1931:
GATE Multi-Concept Sums

Most 2-mark GATE numericals are not hard — they are chains. One concept gives a value, that value feeds a second concept, and the second feeds a third. If you know all three concepts but still get stuck, the gap is not knowledge — it is linking. This book breaks

every multi-concept GATE EE sum (2007–2026) into its chain: ① → ② → ③, then solves it step by step along that chain.

The 4-move chain method

1. TARGET — Underline what is asked. Write the one formula that directly gives it.

2. GAPS — Circle every symbol in that formula that is not given in the question.

3. LINKS — For each gap ask: “which concept produces this value?” (it is often from another chapter). Repeat until every gap is filled by given data. You have just built the chain backwards.

4. RUN — Now solve forwards ① → ② → ③. At the end check units and a limit case (does the answer make sense?).
1932:
Words in the question that tell you which link to use

If the question says…Use this concept as a link
“switch was closed for a long time”, “steady state before t = 0”DC steady state: L = short, C = open → initial value
“at t = 0⁺”, “just after switching”Continuity: iL and vC cannot jump
“time constant”, “after a long time”, “drops to”, “crosses zero”v = V∞ + (V0 − V∞)e−t/τ + natural log
“maximum efficiency”, “at what load”Cu loss = iron loss → x = √(Pi/Pcu,FL)
“same supply”, “V/f constant”, “frequency changed”Φ ∝ V/f, hysteresis ∝ f, eddy ∝ f²
“rated”, “on a base of”, “per unit”Base values: Zbase = kV²/MVA, Ibase = MVA/(√3 kV)
“leading / lagging / unity pf”Phasor diagram: E = V + I·Z (sign of jX·I depends on pf)
“maximum power”, “steady-state limit”Pmax = V₁V₂/X at δ = 90°
“critical clearing”, “fault cleared”Swing curve + equal-area criterion
“firing angle α”, “average output”Vdc formula of the converter + load equation (V = E + IR)
“damping ratio”, “overshoot”, “settling time”Characteristic equation → ζ, ωn → Mp, ts
“steady-state error”, “ramp input”System type + error constant Kp, Kv, Ka
“neglect …”, “ideal …”Drop that element → simpler model (see Cross-Comparison Book, Part F)
1933:
Demo 1 — GATE EE 2019 Q.41 (3 concepts)

Question: A 0.1 μF capacitor charged to 100 V is discharged through a 1 kΩ resistor. The time in ms required for the voltage across the capacitor to drop to 1 V is ____.

①RC time constant

→ τ = RC = 1000 × 0.1×10⁻⁶ = 0.1 ms

②Exponential decay

→ v(t) = 100 e−t/τ = 1

③Natural logarithm

→ t = τ ln(100/1) = 0.1 × 4.605 = 0.46 ms

➜ ➜

How the 4 moves find this chain:

1 · TARGET: time t. The formula that contains t is v = V₀e−t/τ.

2 · GAPS: τ is not given.

3 · LINKS: τ comes from concept ① (τ = RC). To get t out of the exponent you need concept ③ (ln).

4 · RUN: ① → ② → ③ = 0.46 ms. Check: 1 V is 1 % of 100 V → about 4.6 τ (between 4τ = 98.2 % and 5τ = 99.3 % decay). ✔

Trap: using log₁₀ instead of ln gives 0.2 ms.
1934:
Demo 2 — GATE EE 2020 Q.45 (3 concepts)

Question: A resistor and capacitor in series are connected to a 10 V DC supply through a switch closed at t = 0. The capacitor voltage crosses 0 V at t = 0.4τ. Find the absolute percentage change needed in the initial capacitor voltage so that the zero crossing happens at t = 0.2τ.

①General first-order

solution

→ v(t) = V∞ + (V₀ − V∞)e−t/τ, V∞ = 10 V

②Zero-crossing condition

→ 0 = 10 + (V₀ − 10)e−t₁/τ ⇒ V₀ = 10(1 − et₁/τ)

③Percentage change

→ V₀ = −4.918 V (0.4τ), V₀′ = −2.214 V (0.2τ) ⇒ 55 %

➜ ➜

How the 4 moves find this chain:

1 · TARGET: % change in V₀ = |V₀′ − V₀| / |V₀|.

2 · GAPS: both V₀ and V₀′ are unknown.

3 · LINKS: each comes from the zero-crossing condition ② applied to the general solution ①. The final value V∞ = 10 V comes from “capacitor = open in DC steady state”.

4 · RUN: ① → ② (twice) → ③ = (4.918 − 2.214)/4.918 = 55 %. Check: a crossing earlier needs a smaller negative start. ✔

Trap: V₀ must be negative — a capacitor charging towards +10 V only “crosses zero” if it starts below zero.
1935:
Chain patterns that repeat

The same chains come back year after year. Learn these patterns; each topic section below starts with its own pattern table.

TopicMost common chain
TransientsDC steady state (initial value) → Thevenin R (τ) → first-order solution → ln
AC circuitsPhasor impedance → current/voltage phasor → complex power / pf / resonance
Network theoremsKill sources → Rth; open-circuit → Vth → max power / load current
TransformersLoss separation (Ph ∝ f, Pe ∝ f²) or OC/SC data → Req, Xeq → η / regulation
Induction motorsNs & slip → equivalent circuit current → air-gap power → torque / rotor loss
DC machinesE = V ∓ IaRa → N ∝ E/Φ → torque ∝ ΦIa
Synchronous machinesPhasor E = V + jI Xs → load angle δ → P = EV sinδ / Xs
FaultsPer-unit conversion → Thevenin Z at fault → sequence-network connection → If
StabilityPmax for each state → equal-area criterion → critical angle / time
Power electronicsAverage output formula (α, D) → load equation (V = E + IR) → current / power / pf
Control systemsClosed-loop TF → characteristic equation → ζ, ωn or Routh → spec
MeasurementsMeter principle (average / RMS / form factor) → waveform values → reading / error

Every sum now points to the right helper page

Under each solution you will see coloured tags: Calc § = the section of the Calculation Ready-Reckoner (Appendix A) holding the ln / eˣ / √ / trig / dB values that sum needs; Compare grid = the Cross-Comparison grid (Appendix B) that stops you mixing it up with a

look-alike; One concept § = the One Concept, Many Places family (Appendix C) showing the same formula in other subjects. The Concept Index A–Z at the end lists, for every concept, the pages of all sums that use it.
